original_question: Consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with interaction matrix J = beta W where W ~ GOE(n), with an arbitrary external field, and Glauber dynamics for sampling from the Gibbs measure on {+1,-1}^n. Does Glauber dynamics mix in polynomial time for all beta up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1?
target_in_paper: Entry 7, Open Problem 15: whether Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with arbitrary external field mixes in polynomial time up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it is about the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, uses the paper's parametrization J = beta W with W ~ GOE(n), keeps the external field arbitrary, asks specifically about Glauber dynamics rather than a different sampler, and identifies the same threshold beta* = 1 as the target regime.
missing_details: The Gibbs measure should be written explicitly as mu_{J,h}(x) proportional to exp((1/2) x^T J x + h^T x) on {+1,-1}^n, with h in R^n.

The paper's Glauber dynamics is the discrete-time single-site chain: choose i uniformly from [n] and resample X_i from the conditional law mu_{J,h}( . | X_{-i}); your draft names the dynamics but does not spell out this update rule.

The surrounding context defines mixing via the total-variation mixing time T_epsilon, from any starting state, for fixed small epsilon; 'mix in polynomial time' should be tied to that notion to be fully paper-faithful.
All SK statements in Entry 7 are understood with high probability over the disorder W as n -> infinity; your draft omits this quantifier.

The question is specifically about Glauber dynamics itself, not about the existence of some polynomial-time sampling algorithm. This distinction matters because the same paragraph discusses non-Glauber algorithms and weaker Wasserstein guarantees without external field.

The paper leaves the precise GOE(n) normalization implicit, and your draft does too. To stay closest to the paper, it is better to keep the notation W ~ GOE(n) rather than insert a new normalization convention not stated there.

The phrase 'up to the threshold beta* = 1' is informal in the paper; a stand-alone version should indicate the intended asymptotic quantifier, e.g. for each fixed beta up to that threshold and all sufficiently large n.
refined_question: For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising model on {+1,-1}^n with Gibbs measure mu_{J,h}(x) proportional to exp((1/2) x^T J x + h^T x), where h in R^n is arbitrary and J = beta W with W ~ GOE(n), consider the discrete-time single-site Glauber dynamics that at each step chooses i uniformly from [n] and resamples x_i from the conditional law mu_{J,h}( . | x_{-i}). Is it true that, with probability tending to 1 over the disorder W as n -> infinity, the total-variation mixing time T_epsilon of this chain is bounded by n^{O(1)} for every fixed epsilon in (0,1) and every inverse temperature beta up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1?
justification: The exact target in the paper is Open Problem 15 in Entry 7, not a broader question about arbitrary samplers. The preliminaries in Entry 7 define the Gibbs measure mu_{J,h}, specialize to J = beta W with W ~ GOE(n), state that the discussion is with high probability over the disorder W, and define the single-site Glauber chain and total-variation mixing time T_epsilon (Entry 7, p. 10). Open Problem 15 then asks whether this Glauber dynamics fast mixes, meaning polynomial-time mixing, up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1 in the presence of an arbitrary external field (Entry 7, Open Problem 15, p. 11). The nearby context also notes separate results for non-Glauber algorithms and weaker Wasserstein guarantees without external field, so the refined question should stay narrowly on total-variation polynomial mixing of Glauber dynamics itself rather than broaden to general polynomial-time sampling (Entry 7, p. 11).
